title: Same Probabilities, Different Advice: Gain-Loss Framing Effects in High-Stakes LLM Decision Support
abstract: arXiv:2610.29294v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support consequential decisions, yet their reliability under equivalent representations of uncertainty remains unclear. Existing work has documented prompt sensitivity, cognitive biases, and confidence miscalibration, but it is still unknown whether high-stakes advice changes when the same probability is expressed through complementary gain and loss frames. We introduce FrameBench-HPS, a controlled benchmark of 2,880 prompts derived from 240 high-stakes scenarios across healthcare, finance, education/career, and legal/consumer-rights domains. Across seven LLMs, gain-loss framing changes the recommendation category in 32.4% of complete groups, with most changes involving uncertainty rather than direct reversals. Human evaluation confirms corresponding shifts in perceived risk and directiveness. Robustness experiments show that framing effects persist under conversational paraphrases

translated_title: 相同概率，不同建议：高风险LLM决策支持中的收益-损失框架效应
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于支持重大决策，但它们在等价的不确定性表述下的可靠性仍不清楚。现有研究已经记录了提示敏感性、认知偏差和置信度校准失准等问题，但尚不清楚当同一概率通过互补的收益和损失框架表达时，高风险建议是否会发生变化。我们提出了FrameBench-HPS，这是一个受控基准，包含由医疗健康、金融、教育/职业以及法律/消费者权益四个领域的240个高风险场景生成的2,880个提示。在七个大语言模型上，收益-损失框架在32.4%的完整组中改变了推荐类别，其中大多数变化涉及不确定性而非直接的推荐反转。人类评估证实了模型在感知风险和指示性程度上的相应转变。鲁棒性实验表明，框架效应在对话式改写下依然存在。
tldr: 该研究提出FrameBench-HPS基准，揭示了大语言模型在提供高风险决策建议时存在显著的框架效应：即使概率信息在数学上完全等价，收益与损失两种表述方式仍会在32.4%的情况下改变模型的推荐类别。
en_tdlr: This study introduces FrameBench-HPS, a benchmark revealing significant gain-loss framing effects in LLM decision support, where mathematically equivalent probabilities expressed in complementary frames shift high-stakes recommendation categories in 32.4% of cases.
